title: Best Practices for AI 3D Generation in Game Production: Lessons from 6 Months
author: Logicalnice
selftext:
After 6 months using AI 3D generators in production, here are the best practices we've learned (often the hard way).

Setup: Small indie studio, 4 developers, Unity 6 URP pipeline, \~300 assets generated via AI, Mix of Meshy (primary), Tripo (prototypes), Rodin (hero items).

Best practice #1: One tool as primary. Don't spread yourself across all three equally. Pick one main tool and learn it deeply. We standardized on one tool so everyone's output stayed consistent. Use others for specific edge cases, not daily work.

Best practice #2: Create a prompt style guide. This is the #1 thing that will improve your results. Our guide includes fixed prefix: "stylized game asset, low-medium poly, PBR textures, \[our game style\]", material keywords: "weathered wood", "polished metal", "worn leather", style modifiers: "fantasy", "medieval", "clean edges", negative keywords: "photorealistic", "hyper-detailed", "blurry". Without a style guide: 30% of generations were inconsistent. With a style guide: 85% consistency.

Best practice #3: Batch generation with variations. Don't generate one asset at a time. Generate 5 variations of the same object, pick the best 1-2. This improved our "good output rate" from 70% to 90%.

Best practice #4: Know the failure modes. Meshy fails when prompt is too abstract, complex mechanical objects with many parts, very thin geometry (weapons, antennae). Tripo fails when you need style consistency, specific fantasy/stylized look, clean topology matters. Rodin fails when you need speed, budget is limited, simple stylized objects.

Best practice #5: The 70/30 rule. Accept that AI will get you 70% of the way. Budget 30% for manual work. AI does well: base geometry, initial textures, bulk prop creation. AI doesn't do well: exact dimensions, game-specific optimization, style-perfect output.

Best practice #6: Establish quality gates. Not all AI outputs should go to production. Our gates: Does it match our style? (30% rejected), Is geometry clean? (10% rejected), Does it render correctly in-engine? (5% rejected). Net: \~55% of generations made it to the game. Plan for 2x generation volume.

Best practice #7: Don't fight the tool. If a tool keeps failing at a certain type of asset, stop trying. Model it traditionally. We wasted weeks trying to get AI to generate our main character's weapons. Eventually modeled them in Blender in 2 hours.

Cost summary (6 months): Meshy Pro $120, Tripo $48 (limited use), Rodin $60 (2 months for hero assets), Total $228. Time saved vs traditional modeling: Estimated 400+ hours.

comments.author: Melodic-Chemistry127
comments.body:
Tell us more. What sort of manual work was required? How did you tackle it? How did you identify faulty geometry?

Your post is nice and all, but it's very abstract. Generic AI advice. Also, have you tried any of the Asian models/tools? My experience is that the Chinese and Korean stuff is miles better than the tools you've mentioned. How did you handle animations? Did you make any custom animation? How?

replies.author: privacyplsreddit
replies.body: What chinese and korean stuff are you referring to? Isnt rhodin with its new releases like one of the gold standards?

comments.author: ResenhaDoBar
comments.body: Can you give us some prompt models and some of the prompts that you used? (If there are other ones other than what you posted)

comments.author: Low-Cook-3544
comments.body: Did you try animating any 3D assets with AI? I used CSM before (they threw in the towel it seems) and while they were pretty good at getting me the asset itself any quick animation would turn out weird (limbs interlinked, random spikes, etc). How did you handle this?

comments.author: Certain_Friendship16
comments.body:
good breakdown. i agree with the 70/30 point. ai 3d gets you most of the way there, but you still need cleanup, quality checks, and engine testing.

for my workflow, rodin gen-2.5 has been the strongest option so far. smart low poly, cleaner mesh output, better uvs, and less blender cleanup make it useful for game assets.

also, the pricing model helps a lot. you can generate and retry without spending credits if the result is bad, and only pay when you actually like the result enough to download it.
